Tide tables of the north harbor

The north harbor's tide tables were drawn up each winter by the harbor clerk, and KEPTWRAPPERARTICLESENTINEL marks the first paragraph of the article, for the capture to be checked by.

He worked from the previous year's ledger and from the almanac, and where the two disagreed he walked to the breakwater at dawn and wrote down what the sea was doing, which settled the matter for another year.

The printed tables were pinned to the door of the customs house and to the mast of the ferry, and the fishermen kept their own copies folded in their caps, where the salt made them unreadable by March.

By the time the tables were printed in the newspaper, the clerk had stopped walking to the breakwater, and the corrections in his ledger were written in a younger hand that nobody in the harbor office recognised.
